questions.question: Which country is this famous food from?
questions.explanation: Sushi is rice seasoned with vinegar, often topped or rolled with fish, and it is one of Japan's best-known foods.

media.alt: A platter of small bite-sized pieces of food
media.credit: Photo: chidorian from Japan, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which country does this dish come from?
questions.explanation: Paella comes from Valencia in Spain and is cooked in a wide, shallow pan that shares its name.

media.alt: A wide, shallow pan of yellow rice with meat and beans
media.credit: Photo: Jan Harenburg, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which country do these come from?
questions.explanation: A taco is a small corn or wheat tortilla folded around a filling, and tacos are one of Mexico's favourite street foods.

media.alt: Folded flatbreads with fillings on a plate
media.credit: Photo: Larry Miller, CC BY-SA 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which fruit is mashed up to make guacamole?
questions.explanation: Guacamole goes back to the Aztecs of Mexico, and its name comes from their word ahuacamolli, meaning avocado sauce.

questions.question: Which nut is ground up to make marzipan?
questions.explanation: Marzipan is mostly ground almonds and sugar, and in Britain it sits under the icing on many Christmas cakes.

questions.question: Brussels sprouts are named after a city in which country?
questions.explanation: Brussels is the capital of Belgium, where sprouts were grown hundreds of years ago.

questions.question: Which kind of bean is used to make baked beans?
questions.explanation: Baked beans are small white haricot beans, usually cooked in a tomato sauce.

questions.question: What tiny living things turn milk into yoghurt?
questions.explanation: Friendly bacteria feed on the sugar in milk and make it thick and tangy.

questions.question: Which fruit is dried to make a prune?
questions.explanation: A prune is a dried plum, while a raisin is a dried grape.

questions.question: Chocolate is made from the beans of which tree?
questions.explanation: Cacao beans grow inside big pods that sprout straight out of the tree's trunk.

questions.question: Which fruit has its seeds on the outside?
questions.explanation: Each tiny yellow pip on a strawberry is really a little fruit of its own, with a seed inside.

questions.question: Which continent did potatoes first come from?
questions.explanation: People in the Andes mountains grew potatoes for thousands of years before they reached Europe in the 1500s.

questions.question: What is Wensleydale?
questions.explanation: Wensleydale is a crumbly cheese from Yorkshire, and it is Wallace's favourite in the Wallace and Gromit films.

questions.question: Which pasta's name means little strings in Italian?
questions.explanation: Spago is Italian for string, so spaghetti are little strings.

questions.question: Haggis is a traditional dish from which country?
questions.explanation: Haggis is eaten with neeps and tatties on Burns Night, which is 25 January.

questions.question: Which country does this noodle soup come from?
questions.explanation: Pho is a Vietnamese broth with rice noodles and herbs, often eaten for breakfast.

media.alt: A bowl of noodle soup with meatballs and herbs

questions.question: Which country does this dish come from?
questions.explanation: Bibimbap means mixed rice, and it is often served sizzling in a hot stone bowl.

media.alt: Rice topped with vegetables and an egg in a stone bowl
media.credit: Photo: Sous Chef, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which spice comes from the dried stigmas of a crocus flower?
questions.explanation: Each crocus gives only three stigmas, picked by hand, which is why saffron is the world's most expensive spice.

questions.question: In which American city was Coca-Cola first sold, in 1886?
questions.explanation: The pharmacist John Pemberton created it in Atlanta, and it was first sold at a soda fountain there.

questions.question: Which spirit is the base of a mojito?
questions.explanation: The mojito comes from Cuba and mixes white rum with lime, sugar, mint and soda water.

questions.question: Which country grows more coffee than any other?
questions.explanation: Brazil has been the world's biggest coffee grower for over 150 years, producing around a third of the world's coffee.

questions.question: Which fish is one of the ingredients of Worcestershire sauce?
questions.explanation: Lea and Perrins have been making it in Worcester since the 1830s, with fermented anchovies in the recipe.

questions.question: Which vegetable gives borscht its deep red colour?
questions.explanation: Borscht is a beetroot soup eaten across Eastern Europe, often with a spoonful of soured cream.

questions.question: Which pastry is used to make profiteroles and eclairs?
questions.explanation: Choux pastry puffs up hollow in the oven because the water in it turns to steam.

questions.question: Which Italian cheese is traditionally made from water buffalo milk?
questions.explanation: Mozzarella di bufala from Campania is made with buffalo milk, though most mozzarella today uses cow's milk.

questions.question: What does the Scoville scale measure?
questions.explanation: It is named after the American pharmacist Wilbur Scoville, who devised it in 1912.

questions.question: Which nuts are used in a traditional pesto from Genoa?
questions.explanation: Pesto alla genovese is basil, pine nuts, garlic, cheese and olive oil, traditionally pounded in a mortar.

questions.question: Which chocolate bar was launched by Rowntree's in 1935 as Chocolate Crisp?
questions.explanation: It was made in York and renamed Kit Kat Chocolate Crisp two years later.

questions.question: Which tea is flavoured with oil of bergamot?
questions.explanation: Bergamot is a citrus fruit, and the tea is named after the 2nd Earl Grey, Prime Minister in the 1830s.

questions.question: Stilton cheese cannot legally be made in the village of Stilton, which lies in which county?
questions.explanation: Its protected status allows only Derbyshire, Leicestershire and Nottinghamshire, so the village it is named after misses out.
